Battlefield 1 is one of those games that receives a lot of praise, and after playing it I can understand why. The presentation is impressive, the battles feel large in scale and the game does a good job of capturing the atmosphere of World War I. However, once I looked beyond the setting itself, I found a game that offers far less depth than its reputation suggests.

The campaign never managed to hold my attention for very long. Instead of telling a single story, Battlefield 1 is divided into multiple war stories that follow different characters and situations. While this allows the game to showcase different parts of the conflict, it also makes the overall experience feel disconnected. None of the stories felt particularly memorable and, by the end, I was left with the impression that the campaign existed more to showcase the setting than to tell a compelling narrative.

The multiplayer is clearly the main focus, but this is also where many of my criticisms begin. Battlefield 1 follows the same formula that the franchise has relied on for years. Large maps, objective-based modes, infantry combat, tanks and aircraft all return once again. The problem is not that this formula is bad. The problem is that I struggle to see meaningful evolution compared to previous entries.

One of the biggest examples is vehicle gameplay. Battlefield has always promoted large-scale warfare where vehicles play an important role, yet I never felt that the franchise significantly expanded or improved these systems over time. Tanks still feel limited in their design and interactions. I am not asking Battlefield to become a simulator like War Thunder, nor do I expect every vehicle to operate with realistic armor penetration mechanics. What I wanted to see was some form of evolution.

Different vehicles should feel more distinct from one another. Progression could offer more meaningful customization and variety. Vehicle combat could create more situations where players need to think about po…

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering cheaters in multiplayer matches, noting issues with server moderation and admin abuse.

citations.review_text:
In my opinion, this is the best game in the franchise and easily my personal favorite. It's so ridiculously well-made and detailed, which is incredible for a game that's nearly 10 years old now. Even after three subsequent releases, this is still the absolute GOAT of the series.

The good:
- One of the most immersive war games I've ever played. Everything is crafted at a top-tier level—graphics, atmosphere, and audio design.
- Tons of weapons available. While every PvP game has its meta choices and weaker guns, almost everything feels viable and usable.
- Excellent map design. Most maps are extremely fun to play, and I love how accurately they capture real-world historical locations.
- The campaign is really cool and presents a grounded, realistic look at war, even if it is on the shorter side.
- I love that it's set in WWI, which is a rare setting compared to the flood of WWII games.
- The Sentry Kit pickup mechanic adds a great dynamic to matches without feeling broken or unfair.

The neutral:
- Cheaters do exist, and EA isn't going to fix the issue anytime soon. I'm not putting this strictly in "the bad" because the cheater count isn't overwhelming, but it's still worth noting.
- Certain maps feel somewhat unbalanced depending on the game mode, though this is definitely the exception rather than the rule.

The bad:
- A few specific weapons feel noticeably overpowered, which becomes especially frustrating if you play Hardcore mode.
- Infinite vehicle ammo can be annoying. Battlefield V fixed this by forcing vehicles to re-supply at base stations, but here, sweat pilots can stay in the air endlessly, making planes feel oppressive.

This game regularly goes on deep discount during sales, making it an absolute steal. Easy recommendation for anyone looking for a top-tier PvP shooter or historical war game.

Although the game certainly isn't dead, if You're en English speaker, you're be disconnected from Asian servers (which are the closest to us with full lobbies), if you're a good player. More so if you dare mention being shot through walls more than once, once in a game.

The only Australian server that is full during peak play times, have some regulars that use cheats such as wall hacks and aim bot, but it's accepted becuase they're always on the side containing the server owners interests.

The American servers have been fine to play on, with rarely a cheater encountered. 

I've only marked this as a "I do not recommend" game, because there's only a couple of servers where good players are welcome. For a player with only 400 odd hours into the game, hardly ever being able to play some games without either A) cheaters dominating the server for the server admin's interests and/or B) being kicked for being an English speaker, is a demonstration of community servers' interest in the games' future.

If you're cool with all of the above, I recommend. It was a fun 400 hrs, but I will not play it again. Otherwise, spend your money elswhere where you'll have a chance of it being appreciated/respected by the community that you'll be playing amongst.
